properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-29: in the dev_reflow2 hub the bypass nudge told a session "the design graph was never consulted" after it had recorded its change before editing and re-baselined after — because its design calls went through servers the hook's matcher does not name
properties.source: dev_reflow2 hub session 2026-09-28/29; dev_reflow2/.claude/settings.local.json and ~/.claude/settings.json hooks; reflow2 tools/loop_nudge.py PostToolUse branch
properties.statement:
OBSERVED: the Stop hook said "reflow2: 4 file(s) edited this session and the design graph was never consulted". The session had made dozens of design calls: in flo2's hosted design (server `flo2`) it recorded snapshot_before_change BEFORE editing flo2's gateway client and set_artifact_checksum after, plus a root-cause finding; in reflow2's design (server `child-reflow2`) it searched, read and revised findings. The other two edited files were the agent's own memory notes, not design artifacts.
WHY, READ FROM THE CONFIG: both settings files wire PostToolUse to loop_nudge.py with matcher `mcp__reflow2__.*` (plus Edit|Write). The script itself accepts any tool name containing "reflow2" and "__", so `mcp__child-reflow2__*` WOULD count if the hook ran — the matcher stops it running. Hosted designs are named after the design (`flo2`, `graph-primitives`), so no name-based test can recognise them.
CLASS: the nudge identifies "a reflow2 server" by its NAME, but a hub reaches its designs through servers named after those designs, local or hosted. In a hub the bypass nudge therefore fires on exactly the sessions that did the work in the right place, and cannot tell them from a real bypass — the false-positive the requirement's edit-count threshold was meant to bound, arriving by a route the threshold does not see.
NOT ESTABLISHED: whether the Stop-side graph probe (cap:stop-nudge-asks-the-graph) would have answered differently; it asks only this project's own server.
